name: Judgment Labs
tagline: MCP-Native Agent Eval vs SDK-Traced Hosted Agent Judge Platform
oneLine: The continuous-improvement stack for agents. Monitor and improve your agent's behavior at scale.
tldrVendor: Judgment Labs calls Judgment the continuous-improvement stack for agents: the open-source judgeval SDK (Apache-2.0, Python and TypeScript) traces agents into a hosted platform where Agent Judges and Code Judges score traces and track behaviors, with a hosted MCP server for coding agents. The company, Judgment, Inc. of San Francisco, announced a $32M round led by Lightspeed on 2026-05-12; self-hosting is listed as coming soon.

rows.vendor: Python/TypeScript SDK (install judgeval): Tracer.init, Tracer.wrap on provider clients, Tracer.observe on custom code
Hosted platform only; self-hosting is listed as coming soon
rows.quote: Self-hosting capabilities for the Judgment Platform are coming soon.

rows.vendor: In-process SDK built on OpenTelemetry, initialized in every process that creates spans; exports to Judgment
rows.quote: Initialize once in every process that creates spans, before constructing wrapped clients, observed functions, workers, or the application.

rows.vendor: Agent Judge follows a natural-language rubric; Code Judge runs your Python; outputs tracked as behaviors online/offline
rows.quote: An Agent Judge follows a natural-language rubric and reasons over the supplied trace or example.

rows.vendor: Provider instrumentation captures token usage and cost; the traces table exposes a cost column per trace and span
rows.quote: Provider calls, token usage, and cost

rows.vendor: Hosted MCP server (mcp.judgmentlabs.ai) with OAuth for Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, Codex to query traces and judges
rows.quote: The Judgment MCP server gives coding agents authenticated, project-scoped tools for investigating traces, inspecting evaluations, and performing approved actions.

rows.vendor: judgeval SDK is Apache-2.0; the Judgment platform is hosted and proprietary (self-hosting listed as coming soon)

rows.vendor: Not stated in the vendor's documentation as of 2026-09-21
rows.quote: Not stated: The docs index (docs.judgmentlabs.ai/llms.txt) has no security or compliance page. docs.judgmentlabs.ai/documentation/compliance (still titled "Security & Compliance" in search engines, with snippets claiming SOC 2 Type 1 complete and HIPAA) returned 404 on 2026-09-21, as did judgmentlabs.ai/security, judgmentlabs.ai/pricing and the careers page; trust.judgmentlabs.ai redirects to the homepage, which contains no SOC, HIPAA, GDPR, SSO or enterprise strings. Do not publish a compliance claim either way.

vendorReasons.text: You need Agent Judges that apply a natural-language rubric to whole agent trajectories, alongside Code Judges written in Python.
You need production behavior monitoring with detection rates per behavior and alerts when an agent regresses.
You need auto-instrumentation for LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK, Google ADK or Vercel AI SDK with minimal code changes.
You need OpenTelemetry-based tracing with dual export to Judgment and to your existing OTEL backend.
You need offline tests that compare judge and agent versions across a fixed dataset built from production traces.

faq.question: What is the difference between Iris and Judgment Labs?
faq.vendorPart: Judgment Labs describes Judgment as the continuous-improvement stack for agents: its open-source judgeval SDK (Python and TypeScript, Apache-2.0) traces your agent into a hosted platform where Agent Judges and Code Judges score traces and track behaviors.

faq.question: Is Iris better than Judgment Labs for MCP agent evaluation?
faq.vendorPart: Judgment offers things Iris does not: rubric-driven Agent Judges over full trajectories, behavior monitoring with regression alerts, offline tests over datasets built from production traces, and a hosted MCP server that lets coding agents query traces and judges.
